event.summary: Removing failed-capture invalidation does not leave a fallible host screen read untreated
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether removing forget_tail_hinted and fallible capture handling could leave a session stuck waiting after its screen becomes unreadable. Source refutation: ticker.rs:1330-1337 excludes hosts not caught up or without owned-live evidence; hosts/terminal.rs:2229-2247 implements screen_tail and title as infallible reads of the current emulator or its retained view, rather than a subprocess capture that can fail. The new calls therefore have no failed-capture result for the removed handler to handle. SPEC_impl.md, Recovery and checkpoints, states that screen text and title come from a view left in place while encoding, without waiting. This rejects the proposed regression from deletion of tmux capture-failure handling; races after the live-set snapshot and unrelated runtime defects are not established by this check. Suggested bucket: other if it existed. Confidence: confirmed source refutation; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation as above. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no; the considered consequence is stale cosmetic status, without an established security or loss-of-work route.

event.summary: Host-only sampling preserves the prior successful-sample baseline and encoding view
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Synthesis confirms that removing tmux capture-failure invalidation did not introduce a host baseline or encoding-view regression. Original considered consequence retained: a session might keep stale waiting evidence, or date/reorder activity after a failed read without the reset that formerly discarded the baseline. Checks/results: parent-revision ticker.rs:1712-1719 already applies exactly the caught_up plus owned-live filter now at :1330-1337; parent terminals.rs:319-339 already returns Ok(host.screen_tail(max_bytes)) and Ok(host.title()), so production host reads never reached the failed-capture reset. The fault injection removed by this patch was a test seam, not a production host read failure. At the reviewed revision hosts/terminal.rs:1429-1454 captures the emulator's real screen/title in View, :1707-1723 and :3589-3605 replace the live slot with that view during encoding, and :2275-2284 reads the live emulator or retained view under the same short mutex without waiting for an encode. The view is the processed emulator state, not evidence of new terminal output or proof of current wall-time liveness; this check does not claim otherwise. ticker.rs:586-629 still supplies no prior reading to a run's first successful sample, keeps Unknown from replacing the stored reading, and establishes transition readiness only on a definite sample; :288-319 requires both prior and fresh readings before activity dating or burst starts. Thus the same baseline/activity rules apply before and after the dispatch simplification. SPEC_impl.md, Status heuristics / Last-activity timestamp / Work-start ordering (:4321-4429), defines successful-sample evidence, first-sample baseline suppression and owned sample counts; Recovery and checkpoints (:2179 onward) explicitly describes the encoding view. These source checks independently support the caller-provided g134/l2 interface result. Suggested bucket: other for the considered cosmetic status claim; no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed source refutation; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation of a regression introduced by this patch, with identical prior production host reads and filter. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no for this considered claim. Caveats: does not adjudicate separate pre-existing host gap/re-adoption behavior or every status heuristic; residual documentation of the removed reset is recorded independently under c3.

event.summary: Removed tmux ticker work has no remaining supported terminal to observe
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether removing pane-death wakes, pane-map observation, tmux-tab reaping and old-terminal-warning reconciliation leaves legacy sessions without the periodic behavior they still require. Source refutation: service/terminals.rs:1-7 and 122-141 resolve runtime terminals as HostTerminal, and 175-176 documents old-kind rows as ended at startup. service/core/old_terminals.rs:1-10 and 159-168 implement the replacement startup boundary; its module docs describe conversion and sweeping before ordinary operation. SPEC_impl.md:2882-2891, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, explicitly says: 'This release ends them at startup (below); every terminal runs in a terminal host' and 'The running supervisor runs no tmux at all, and its driver of the old terminals is gone'. SPEC.md:2804-2814 says the old warning is replaced by a startup notice and existing warnings are resolved at startup. The removed ticker routines are therefore not needed to service a supported legacy terminal. This is a removal/interface check, not a review or approval of the separate startup termination policy or its accepted failure residuals. Suggested bucket: other for the considered missing-periodic-work claim. Confidence: confirmed source/contract refutation; no execution. proposed_drop: the retained runtime uses only HostTerminal and the quoted specification retires the old ticker responsibilities. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no for this considered claim; no path from ticker removal to killing user work was established or asserted.

event.summary: Old-terminal warning resolution moved to startup rather than disappearing with ticker work
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Synthesis confirms that deleting the ticker's old-terminal-warning and tmux observation work does not omit a continuing responsibility for supported terminals. Original considered consequence retained: legacy sessions could lose needed status/death/tab-reap updates or old-terminal warnings could remain unresolved after the periodic reconciliation is removed. Checks/results: service/terminals.rs:122-141 returns HostTerminal and its :175-176 identifies old tmux rows as ended by startup. service/core.rs:6142-6184 calls old-terminal termination before reload; :7080-7090 invokes old_terminals::record_ended for writable reloads even when the converted/ended list is empty. service/core/old_terminals.rs:525-546 records the new OldTerminalEnded notices separately and then resolves all OldTerminal warnings unconditionally with respect to ended-list membership; resolution failure is logged, and :522-524 documents retry at a later start. A complete supervisor-src reference search finds no remaining OldTerminal warning producer or reconcile_old_terminal_notifications call, only the startup resolver, enum compatibility and documentation. Exact contract: SPEC.md:2807 says 'no warning is recorded any more, and every supervisor start marks any unresolved one resolved'; :2811-2813 separately says nothing resolves the new notice. SPEC_impl.md:2883-2891 states 'This release ends them at startup (below); every terminal runs in a terminal host' and 'The running supervisor runs no tmux at all, and its driver of the old terminals is gone'. Those contracts and callers support retiring the ticker responsibilities while preserving the startup-only distinction between resolved warnings and persistent new notices. Suggested bucket: other for the considered missing periodic reconciliation claim. Confidence: confirmed source/contract refutation; no execution. proposed_drop: the claimed continuing ticker responsibility is refuted by the new terminal type and the cited startup resolver/contract. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no for this considered claim; no route from this ticker deletion to killing user work is asserted. Caveats: does not judge or propose dropping a separate finding about startup termination's destructive policy, accepted cleanup failure residuals or database-failure behavior; those are distinct from whether the removed periodic warning/reap code is still required.

event.summary: Sampler field documentation still promises the deleted capture-failure reset
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: The sampler's current lifecycle documentation tells future maintainers that failed reads clear prompt evidence and reset the activity baseline, but this change deletes the only operation that did that. This is a documentation correctness defect; no current runtime regression is claimed. Details: ticker.rs:373-375 promises workspace_trust_prompt is 'cleared on failed capture', :411-416 describes reading falling back after 'a failed capture withdrew what the last screen showed', and :422-431 declares transition_ready 'False for a new or reloaded run and after a failed capture' and links that reset to suppressing activity/reordering after recovery. The assigned patch deletes ActivitySample::forget_tail and forget_tail_hinted, which previously fulfilled those statements. At the reviewed revision a complete src search for transition_ready finds only its declaration (:432), read (:609), and assignment to true (:614); Default at :364-365 and new/reloaded/replacement constructors establish its initial false state. The retained sampler skips unavailable/replaying hosts (:1327-1337), and infallible host screen reads have no failed-capture reset event. These comments are present-tense field contracts and explanatory baseline guarantees, not explicitly historical context. They should describe the actual retained lifecycle or explicitly label the retired tmux behavior as history. Original considered consequence retained: a future maintainer can rely on a nonexistent failure-recovery reset when reasoning about prompt hints and activity ordering. The earlier rationale that runtime harm had not been shown was insufficient to dismiss inaccurate documentation. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source, including all transition_ready references; no execution. proposed_drop: false; parent owns coverage/filter judgment. possible_cover: none known, coverage sources not searched. Could-be-highest: no; this is an inaccurate internal lifecycle description, with no established security or loss-of-work route. Caveat: this does not assert the removed reset is needed by the host-only implementation, nor that host encoding/unavailability currently fabricates activity; c1 separately refutes that regression claim.

event.summary: Removing the observer capture budget does not unbound retained host capture waits
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether changing observe_entries from observe_entry_with_capture_budget to observe_entry removes a per-pass bound and lets many failed launch excerpts delay the fleet's ticker work. Source refutation: parent service/launch_artifacts.rs:72-98 handles Terminal::Host before testing capture_available, appends only a processed-final-screen excerpt using host.screen_tail, and returns; its :67-70 explicitly says 'A host terminal's read is in memory, cannot fail, and is not budgeted.' Only the later tmux capture arm consumes the shared failure budget. The replacement append_launch_excerpt at the reviewed revision uses the same host final-evidence guard and screen_tail call. Thus removing this budget from ticker.rs:1129-1130 removes no bound previously applied to the retained host path. The observer still batches generation-fenced transitions after classification (:1174 onward). Suggested bucket: other for the considered background-work bound; no demonstrated user degradation. Confidence: confirmed source comparison only; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, the eliminated budget never applied to production host excerpts. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route. Caveat: this does not certify every possible resource cost of rendering a large host screen or auditing the excerpt reducer; those are separate implementation concerns, not introduced by this ticker budget deletion.

event.summary: Deleting pane-death publication does not remove terminal-host attachment death evidence
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether deleting the ticker's publish_pane_deaths call and helper could make terminal-host attachments lose final-output or exit notification. Source refutation: parent service/terminals.rs:1989-1997 dispatches AttachBackend::observed_death exclusively to the Tmux pane-death latch, returning None for AttachBackend::Host. The removed helper only iterates attachment backends through that method; it therefore never published host attachment death evidence. Grid streams have their own host subscription, identified at reviewed service/grid_stream.rs:387, and their own exit mapping (:901 onward), independently of the deleted pane latch. This rejects an additional retained-host attachment consequence of the ticker deletion. Suggested bucket: other for the unestablished missed-exit display claim. Confidence: confirmed parent dispatch refutation; no runtime execution. proposed_drop: the removed publisher never handled Host attachments. possible_cover: none; no prohibited coverage source read. Caveat: this is a removal/interface check, not a comprehensive grid-stream correctness audit or a proposed drop of the separate intentional old-tmux history loss reported by interface groups.
